task: nl-gap item half of a-p-item: the item identity the inventory rows resolve, and the item-spawn / pickup-sync entries

assembly.note: the same image evidence/inventory-actions.json and evidence/w1-native-world-paths.json were produced against

itemIdentity.nativeNumber: ItemDataBlock.persistentID — the value pItemData.itemID_gearCRC carries for a non-gear item
itemIdentity.table: GameData.ItemDataBlock : GameDataBlockBase<ItemDataBlock>, whose static block table is the only authority on which item ids exist: `ItemDataBlock.GetBlock(uint)` answers the block, and the block's own `persistentID` and `inventorySlot` are read back from it
itemIdentity.spelling: an authored `forge.resource.item` id is the official persistent id as plain decimal text — the spelling this runtime already pins for an authored native block id (the enemy domain's `enemy-type` mount and its `v-e-type` read row both carry EnemyDataBlock.persistentID as decimal text). `WeaponSupplyItems.TryResolve` parses it with NumberStyles.None, refuses `0`, a text longer than ten digits, anything that is not a decimal integer, and a table that answers a block whose own id differs from the one asked for
itemIdentity.slotNarrowing: `WeaponSupplyItems.TryResolvePocketItem` answers only for a block whose own `inventorySlot` is `InventorySlot.InPocket`; `PlayerBackpackManager.MasterAddItem` places the item in the slot its pItemData names, so a resource pack or a consumable added as a pocket item would sit in a slot the game never reads it from. The narrow answer refuses such a resource instead of misplacing it
itemIdentity.stillMissing: giving a gear-slot item (a resource pack, a consumable, a weapon or a tool) needs the game's own gear path — PlayerBackpackManager.MasterAddItem(Item, SNet_Player) over an instance built by ItemReplicationManager.SpawnItem — and that half is not implemented by this batch

spawnEntry.entry: ItemReplicationManager.SpawnItem(pItemData data, delItemCallback callback, ItemMode mode, Vector3 position, Quaternion rotation, AIG_CourseNode courseNode, PlayerAgent owner)
spawnEntry.source: evidence/inventory-actions.json (a-inv1) decodes this class; the entry spawns a level instance from a pItemData the caller builds
spawnEntry.whyNotUsedForGive: it spawns a world object rather than moving an instance into a backpack, and it takes an `owner` only to attribute the placement; a give that used it would leave the item on the floor

pickupEntry.entry: LG_PickupItem_Sync.AttemptPickupInteraction(ePickupItemInteractionType, SNet_Player, pItemData_Custom, Vector3, Quaternion, AIG_CourseNode, bool, bool)
whyNotUsable: it is the synced state machine's own transition, reached through the SNet state replicator's delegate, and has no literal caller in the image
the caller supplies the interaction type and the placement data the replicator handed it, so it is not a host API
the catalog's `items` input names world item entities and this build has no entity kind for a world item, so a plan cannot name one

spawnAndPickup.conclusion: the give and consume rows keep the host entry points a-inv1 evidenced (`MasterAddItem` and `TryMasterRemovePocketItemWithID`, both of which send the inventory packet in the body they apply in); the item-spawn and pickup-sync entries are real but are world-object paths, so they are not the give row's entry and no second implementation is built from them

cases: the decimal id of a pocket item resolves
a gear-slot block resolves but is not a pocket item
a block whose id differs from the one asked for is refused
a throwing table is a resource this process cannot name
the zero id is never an item

unverified: which spelling the website's export will write for an `forge.resource.item` reference was not decided by this batch: the decimal-persistent-id spelling is the one this runtime already uses for authored block ids, and a resource registry that lands later replaces this narrowing with its own answer
no game process ran: no give or consume was executed against a live backpack
